title: GPS station velocities: east, north and up for some 22,000 continuous GNSS stations, by the MIDAS estimator, from the Nevada Geodetic Laboratory
provider: Nevada Geodetic Laboratory, University of Nevada, Reno (G. Blewitt, W. C. Hammond, C. Kreemer)
credit: GPS velocities: Nevada Geodetic Laboratory (MIDAS, IGS20)

frame.description: the frame: IGS (IGS20, aligned with ITRF2020), or a plate held fixed (NA, EU, PA, ...)

format: Text, one station a line, 27 columns separated by spaces (midas.readme.txt): 1 station; 2 version; 3-4 first and last epoch (decimal year); 5 duration (years); 6-8 numbers of epochs and pairs; 9-11 east, north, up velocity (m/yr); 12-14 their uncertainties (m/yr); 15-17 offsets at the first epoch (m); 18-20 fractions of outliers; 21-23 standard deviations of the pairs' velocities; 24 number of steps; 25-27 latitude, longitude (degrees; longitudes from -360 to 0) and height (m).
coverage: Global, wherever continuous GNSS stations have run for long enough; updated daily
licence: No licence is stated; the data are supplied as is (https://geodesy.unr.edu/Disclaimer.php). The laboratory asks that its products be cited as Blewitt, Hammond and Kreemer (2018), and MIDAS as Blewitt et al. (2016); many stations have an original data citation of their own.
citation: Blewitt, G., Hammond, W. C. and Kreemer, C. (2018), Harnessing the GPS data explosion for interdisciplinary science, Eos 99, doi:10.1029/2018EO104623; Blewitt, G., Kreemer, C., Hammond, W. C. and Gazeaux, J. (2016), MIDAS robust trend estimator for accurate GPS station velocities without step detection, J. Geophys. Res. Solid Earth 121, 2054-2068, doi:10.1002/2015JB012552.
